sentences.text: Pachycephalosaurus wyomingensis is the sole species within the extinct genus Pachycephalosaurus, a marginocephalian dinosaur belonging to the family Pachycephalosauridae.
The animal is known mainly from a single skull and thick skull roofs measuring 22 cm, with estimates of its length at 4.5 meters and weight between 370 and 450 kilograms.
It was a bipedal creature with long strong legs and small five-fingered hands.
A large bony dome on its skull reached up to 25 cm in thickness, serving to cushion the brain.
The bony spikes located on the snout were likely blunted rather than sharp.
This dinosaur is the largest known pachycephalosaur, distinguished by an extremely thick, slightly domed skull roof.
Evidence of cranial pathologies in a specimen suggests the animal engaged in aggressive behavior.
A partial skull was discovered in 1930 by George Fryer Sternberg in the Lance Formation of Niobrara County, Wyoming.
Fossils of this taxon have been found in Montana, South Dakota, Wyoming, and Alberta.
American paleontologist Joseph Leidy named the taxon Tylosteus ornatus seventy-one years before Pachycephalosaurus was described, based on a bone fragment he interpreted as reptile armor.
The genus Pachycephalosaurus was formally established by Brown and Schlaikjer in 1943.
Pachycephalosaurus possessed very small, ridged teeth that were ineffective for chewing tough, fibrous plants.
The most complete fossil jaw shows serrated, blade-like front teeth reminiscent of carnivorous theropods.
It is suspected that the dinosaur may have included meat in its diet.
The skull structure suggests Pachycephalosaurus used its dome as a battering ram for defense or intraspecific combat, similar to modern bighorn sheep or muskoxen.
A 2013 study found that 22% of examined pachycephalosaur domes had lesions consistent with osteomyelitis, supporting the use of domes in combat.
Histological examination reveals that pachycephalosaurid domes are made of fibrolamellar bone containing fibroblasts critical for wound healing.
Research by Cary Woodruff noted that the spine, pelvis, and tail of Pachycephalosaurus resemble those of kangaroos rather than head-butting animals.
Pachycephalosaurus names the clade Pachycephalosauria, a group of herbivorous ornithischian dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous of North America and Asia.
The genus Tylosteus is considered synonymous with Pachycephalosaurus.
In 2009, Horenr and Goodwin proposed that Stygimoloch and Dracorex are juvenile growth stages of Pachycephalosaurus and should be classified as synonyms.
Pachycephalosaurus lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period in western North America, shortly before the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.
Pachycephalosaurus coexisted with diverse dinosaurs including ceratopsians, ankylosaurids, nodosaurids, and theropods like Tyrannosaurus.
The hypothesis that Pachycephalosaurus used its skull dome for head-butting has been disputed in recent years.
In 1990, W. P. Coombs suggested a tooth found by Hatcher came from a pachycephalosaurid, possibly Pachycephalosaurus.
In 2007, researchers proposed that related genera Stygimoloch and Dracorex were juvenile or female forms of Pachycephalosaurus.
